title: Derived reconstruction of the v1.2 core implementation artifact

acceptance_gates.description: A replacement core artifact exists under docs/spec/ with per-declaration provenance tagging, and no element is presented as recovered v1.2 specification text.
The reconstructed DDL is executable against PostgreSQL 18 with pgvector, and all 25 tables named by v1.2 materialize.

v1.2 hard invariants are enforced by the schema rather than described in prose: the event store rejects UPDATE and DELETE; RLS is enabled and forced on every tenant-scoped table; tenant context fails closed; child rows cannot reference a parent owned by another workspace; a risk-3/4 tool execution cannot be recorded without an approval; a promoted tool version cannot lack an immutable digest; and a mutation cannot reach promoted with a null approver. Recording an approver is a structural guard against accidental or unattended promotion, not an authorization boundary: the foreign key proves the user exists, not that the user approved. Binding promotion to an authenticated approval path is an outstanding decision.

Every declaration without source support is enumerated in the artifact's traceability section, generated from the [DECISION] tags in the executable schema so the list cannot drift from it, and the artifact explicitly does not close SRC-001 or unblock FND-DB-DOMAIN.

rollback: Revert the docs/spec commits and the derived-core-schema workflow. No production schema, migration, or cloud resource is created by this package, so rollback has no data implications.
